assumptions: The GitHub webhook payload includes the standard issue object with title, body, labels, number, and user fields.
The Linear integration has access to the Triage team and can create issues within it.
The Linear API create issue endpoint accepts title, description, labels, and reporter as valid fields.
The 'bug' label on GitHub is the exact trigger condition and will not require case-insensitive matching unless specified by the webhook configuration.

issue.title: Fix login button alignment
issue.body: The login button is misaligned on mobile devices. Needs CSS adjustment.

notes: The webhook must be configured to subscribe to the 'issues' event.
The payload includes an 'action' field; for label additions, action will be 'labeled'.
The 'labels' array contains objects with 'name', 'color', 'description', etc.; extract label names via mapping.
Signature verification using X-Hub-Signature-256 header is required for security.
The endpoint must respond with a 2xx status within 10 seconds.
HTTPS is required for the webhook URL in production.
The X-GitHub-Delivery header can be used as an idempotency key.
The 'labeled' action is not the only way labels change; 'opened' may also include labels if the issue is created with labels.
Empty label arrays can occur in non-label-related events (e.g., review_request_removed) due to out-of-order delivery; do not rely on labels array alone for state.

example.query: mutation IssueCreate { issueCreate(input: { title: "Fix login button alignment", description: "The login button is misaligned on mobile devices. Needs CSS adjustment.", teamId: "TRIAGE_TEAM_ID", labels: ["bug"], assigneeId: "REPORTER_USER_ID" }) { success issue { id title description labels { nodes { name } } assignee { id name } } } }

issue.title: Fix login button alignment
issue.description: The login button is misaligned on mobile devices. Needs CSS adjustment.

notes: The Linear API uses GraphQL; the endpoint is https://api.linear.app/graphql.
Authentication is via Bearer token in the Authorization header.
The issueCreate mutation requires at least title and teamId; description, labels, and assigneeId are optional.
Labels are specified as an array of strings (label names) in the input.
The assigneeId should correspond to a Linear user; mapping from GitHub username may require a lookup or predefined mapping.
The teamId must be the UUID of the Triage team; this should be configured as an environment variable or looked up via the teams query.
Changes made in the first 3 minutes after creation are considered part of the creation process and not logged in activity.
The response includes the created issue's id, title, description, labels, and assignee if successful.
Error handling: check for errors array in the response; partial success is possible.
Rate limiting applies; monitor headers and handle 429 responses.

The identifier (GitHub issue number) and reporter (GitHub username) are not standard fields in Linear; they must be stored in description, labels, or custom fields if needed. The plan maps them to identifier and reporter, but Linear does not have these as default fields—notes indicate they may need to be included in description or handled via extensions.
